plan.nickname: Late Mail (a coach named Rumi that once because she never threw first and always got there in the end)
plan.detail: The group chat message 'honestly I'd rather fight anyone with a pulse' was sent by Rumi at 11:52 pm on 3 March, with 14 thumbs-up reactions, two of them from Tamsin's own cornerman, Dele
plan.hands: Rumi keeps turning her phone face-up to check the time and then face-down again on the table; Tamsin works her thumbnail under the edge of an old strip of tape on the table's edge and peels it off a little at a time

candidates.text: What time is it. Dele held my pads for two years, Tamsin. He used to call out what you'd throw next. He was never wrong once.
You've been correct for eleven years. Nobody ever bought a ticket to watch somebody be correct.
I didn't mean you. I meant the division. You're just what was left over when I scrolled down.
Fourteen people liked it. Count them. Your coach liked it twice. He un-liked it and then liked it again.
Bring your notebook. I'll sign the page where you wrote down how to beat me.

chosen_line: Fourteen people liked it. Count them. Your coach liked it twice. He un-liked it and then liked it again.
